identifier: N. Sultanova, S. Kasarova, I. Nikolov, "Dispersion Properties of Optical Polymers", Acta Physica Polonica A 116(4), 585-587 (2009). Proceedings of the International School and Conference on Photonics, PHOTONICA09. DOI 10.12693/APhysPolA.116.585. Polystyrene is the row labelled PS in the table on p. 586.
grade_rule: E3, grade_tag peer_reviewed. A measurement published by another laboratory: 10.3 rule 1's 'a run elsewhere is not a run here' caps it at E3 no matter how carefully it was made. Within E3 the sort ranks peer_reviewed above vendor_spec, so this outranks a data sheet on the same quantity.
license_note: Numeric table values and stated measurement conditions only. No text, figure or curve is reproduced.
method_as_stated: Deviation-angle method on a V-type SF3 glass prism (VoF3) with a Carl Zeiss Jena Pulfrich refractometer PR2, plus a goniometric setup with interference filters and a photodetector. Samples were plates 2.5 to 5.5 mm thick. Silicon oil of nD 1.5601 was used as contacting immersion. Measuring temperature maintained at 20 degC by thermostat, regulation stable to 0.2 degC. The paper states the accuracy of the OP indices as +/-0.001.
why_this_and_not_the_database: refractiveindex.info carries a Sellmeier fit to this same polystyrene data, fitted by Polyanskiy, and is the first result for any search on this quantity. It is a database reproducing a source, which rule 5 keeps out: only the real source is entered. The distinction is not pedantry here -- the fit is somebody's model of the measurement and the paper prints the measurement, and a fit evaluated at a wavelength between table points would deliver an interpolation this store is not allowed to perform.
note: READ FROM THE PRINTED TABLE, NOT FROM A CURVE. The paper carries dispersion charts as well (Figs. 1-3), and a value read off a rendered plot by a model is E6 and may enter nothing (5.3). Every number entered from this source comes from the numeric table on p. 586.
not_entered: The Cauchy-Schott coefficients. The paper describes computing six dispersion coefficients with their OptiColor program and states the approximation is good to 1e-4, but it does NOT print the coefficients for polystyrene. So the dispersion RELATION cannot be entered from this source, only the measured points, and a caller wanting a wavelength between them has a condition_mismatch rather than a value.
caveat: BULK POLYSTYRENE, NOT MICROSPHERES. The samples were moulded plates. Polystyrene beads are the same polymer but not the same object -- a bead carries surface functionalisation, and this laboratory's are carboxyl-modified (tracer_particle_material_and_shape). A microsphere-specific reference exists, Ma, Lu, Ceballos, Wang, Alfano, Phys. Med. Biol. 48, 4165 (2003), which measures polystyrene microspheres from 370 to 1610 nm; it has NOT been obtained or entered, and remains the better source if the difference turns out to matter.
